file_roles.evidence: Two Galera-only branches ran for every transaction. 'if (c_lock)' in lock_table_create becomes 'if (c_lock && wsrep_on_trx(trx))', and 'if (trx->lock.was_chosen_as_deadlock_victim)' in lock_table_enqueue_waiting becomes 'if (trx->lock.was_chosen_as_deadlock_victim && wsrep_on_trx(trx))'. The commit states it plainly, that 'InnoDB executed code that is mean to execute only when Galera is used'.
The identical two guards added to the XtraDB copy of the same lock manager, same functions, same conditions.

rationale: The spurious DB_DEADLOCK is returned by the branch the fix guards, so the error and its cause are the same statement. The reporter's framing is correct and useful, that this 'appears to be a false deadlock detection' seen on no other server, 'This does not occur on any version of MySQL, nor the Ubuntu version 10.0 of MariaDB', which matches a Galera-conditional path being taken on a build where Galera is not in use.
notes: The pasted log belongs to Bacula, not MariaDB: 'localhost-dir: sql_create.c:837-5 Fill File table Query failed: ... ERR=Deadlock found when trying to get lock'. It even carries a file and line reference, sql_create.c:837, which is a Bacula source location while looking exactly like MariaDB's own sql/ naming convention, so it is an actively misleading pointer rather than merely an absent one. That is the fourth instance where the pasted log comes from outside the repository, after GROOVY-3685, KAFKA-6052 and KEYCLOAK-2362. Which of the two engine copies the reporter was running cannot be determined, so both are labelled causal, as in MDEV-12609 and HBASE-10330. The commit also records that 'No always repeatable test case for this issue is known'.
